proof.text: Put $P(U)=R(U)\otimes_{R'(U)}F(U)$, with restrictions induced by those of $R$, $R'$ and $F$. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the target $T=R\otimes_{R'}F$ is the module sheafification $P^\#$; denote its canonical map by $\theta:P\to T$. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\theta$ is additive and $R'$-linear. Define $u_U(m)=\theta_U(1\otimes m)$. Tensor additivity and balancing give $1\otimes(am)=q(a)\otimes m=a(1\otimes m)$ for $a\in R'(U)$, so $u_U$ is $R'(U)$-linear for the specified restricted action. Restrictions send $1\otimes m$ to $1\otimes m|_V$, since restriction maps of rings preserve $1$. Thus the $u_U$ form exactly the asserted morphism of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules): tensor construction and its unit

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ and $t\in T(U)$. The underlying abelian sheaf of the module sheafification $P^\#$ is the abelian sheafification, by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Apply [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] to this abelian presheaf: the underlying map $|\theta|$ is also set sheafification, with the same unit. Now [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and $x_i\in P(U_i)$ such that $t|_{U_i}=\theta_{U_i}(x_i)$. Its universe hypothesis holds because the site is small in the coefficient universe; one can regard the site and its arrows in that common universe. No hypothesis of enough points is used.

source.place: Tag 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), clause (gamma), and Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), first assertion

proof.text: On each $U_i$ write $x_i=\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}r_{ij}\otimes m_{ij}$ with $r_{ij}\in R(U_i)$ and $m_{ij}\in F(U_i)$. This is the elementary presentation of the sectionwise tensor product in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: its additive group is generated by the symbols $r\otimes m$ modulo the additive and balanced relations, so every element is a finite integral combination of these symbols, and integral coefficients can be absorbed into the second factor. The case $n_i=0$ is the zero tensor and already has lift $0\in F(U_i)$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise algebraic tensor product and its defining additive and balanced relations

proof.text: Fix $i$. Use local surjectivity of $q$ to lift $r_{i1}$ on a covering of $U_i$. On each member restrict the remaining $r_{ij}$ and use local surjectivity again to lift $r_{i2}$, retaining the restricted first lift. Induct on $j\leq n_i$. The composite families are coverings by the transitivity axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus on a covering $\{V_{i\alpha}\to U_i\}$ all coefficients lift simultaneously to $a_{ij\alpha}\in R'(V_{i\alpha})$. On each member set $m_{i\alpha}=\sum_j a_{ij\alpha}(m_{ij}|_{V_{i\alpha}})$. The balanced and additive relations of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give $1\otimes m_{i\alpha}=\sum_jq(a_{ij\alpha})\otimes(m_{ij}|_{V_{i\alpha}})=x_i|_{V_{i\alpha}}$. Applying $\theta$ yields $u(m_{i\alpha})=t|_{V_{i\alpha}}$. Compose with the covering of step 2. This proves local surjectivity of $u$. When $n_i=0$, use the identity covering and lift $0$; an empty covering imposes no further condition.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), balancing; sites.tex Tag 00VH (definition-site), transitivity of coverings; explicit argument supplying the quotient step omitted in Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.4(1)

proof.text: To prove the categorical epimorphism assertion directly, take two morphisms $b,c:T\to G$ of $R'$-module sheaves with $b\circ u=c\circ u$. For $t\in T(U)$, use the covering and lifts from step 4. Naturality gives $b_U(t)|_{V_{i\alpha}}=b_{V_{i\alpha}}(u(m_{i\alpha}))=c_{V_{i\alpha}}(u(m_{i\alpha}))=c_U(t)|_{V_{i\alpha}}$. The uniqueness clause of the sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] implies $b_U(t)=c_U(t)$. This applies also to an empty covering, when the section set of $G$ on that object has only one element. Since this holds for every $U,t$, the component maps, and hence the module morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], are equal. This is right cancellation, so $u$ is epic in the required category.

title: tensor quotient epimorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, small in a universe containing the coefficients [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $q:R'\to R$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings that is locally surjective: every section of $R$ lifts to $R'$ after a covering of its domain. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $R'$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form the sheaf tensor product $R\otimes_{R'}F$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and regard it as an $R'$-module via $q$. Then the canonical $R'$-linear map
$$F\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R'}F,\qquad m\longmapsto1\otimes m,$$
is locally surjective and is an epimorphism of sheaves of $R'$-modules.
